'''OpenDraft''' is a [[free and open-source software|free and open-source]] [[screenwriting software|screenwriting application]] developed by Proteus Technologies and released under the [[MIT License]].<ref name="repo" /> It formats scripts to screenplay conventions and includes story-planning, revision and production tools, and runs as a desktop application on [[macOS]], [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]] and [[Linux]], as a mobile application on [[Android (operating system)|Android]] and [[iOS]], and in a [[web browser]].<ref name="website" />

== History ==
The first public version of OpenDraft was released on [[GitHub]] in March 2026.<ref name="releases" /> Version 2.0 followed in September 2026.<ref name="releases" /> The project follows an [[open-core model]]: the core application is MIT-licensed, while a separate proprietary edition adds commercial features through the core's plugin interface.<ref name="repo" />

<!-- ADD INDEPENDENT SOURCE: launch coverage, reviews, or articles about the project -->

== Features ==
OpenDraft's editor applies standard screenplay formatting to scene headings, action, character cues, dialogue, parentheticals, transitions and shots, with autocompletion of character names and scene headings.<ref name="features" /> Besides feature-film screenplays it supports formats for scripted podcasts and comic-book scripts, and can number elements such as scenes, lines of dialogue or sound cues.<ref name="features" />

Story-planning tools include a beat board of [[index card]]s, plotlines with a story timeline, and character profiles with reference images.<ref name="features" /> A "Table Read" feature reads the script aloud with a separate [[speech synthesis|synthesized voice]] for each character, using the device's own voices, an on-device neural voice model, or third-party speech services.<ref name="features" />

The application keeps a built-in version history in which drafts can be checked in, compared side by side and restored, and can write timestamped backup files to a folder chosen by the user.<ref name="features" /> Production features include production tagging, scene, character, location and breakdown reports exportable as [[comma-separated values|CSV]] or [[PDF]], watermarked and password-protected PDF output, and sides.<ref name="features" />

=== Collaboration ===
Writers can edit a script together in real time, with live cursors, presence indicators and per-collaborator permissions (co-edit, suggest or read only). A suggest mode records proposed changes for the author to accept or reject. The collaboration server can be self-hosted.<ref name="features" />

=== File formats ===
OpenDraft imports and exports [[Final Draft (software)|Final Draft]] (<code>.fdx</code>), [[Fountain (markup language)|Fountain]], [[Fade In (software)|Fade In]], Open Screenplay Format and [[Office Open XML|Microsoft Word]] (<code>.docx</code>) files, exports PDF and imports screenplay PDFs back into editable elements, and imports files from Highland, [[WriterDuet]] and [[Celtx]].<ref name="features" /> Its native <code>.odraft</code> format stores a script together with its notes, tags, beats, character profiles and images.<ref name="features" />

== Technology ==
The interface is written in [[TypeScript]] with [[React (software)|React]] and the [[ProseMirror]]-based Tiptap editor. Desktop and mobile builds are packaged with [[Tauri (software framework)|Tauri]] and store projects in a local [[SQLite]] database; the browser version uses a [[Python (programming language)|Python]] [[FastAPI]] backend. Real-time collaboration is built on the [[Yjs]] [[conflict-free replicated data type|CRDT]] library through the Hocuspocus server.<ref name="repo" />
